kind: Independent exact-head public carryless-addend integration review
head: a69a992042d63e58abefd2ae96eb5c4ebd90bb84
checks: The C++ mode defaults to0, admits only0/1/2, and nonzero modes require native CLMAD. Existing CUDA13.3/sm80 guards and host software simulation remain in force.
Public Make passes the enum define once through DEFS and forwards it into the dedicated host arithmetic target. The RTX preset does not enable a nonzero mode.
Public runtime and arithmetic markers are respectively packed carryless addends and packed arithmetic carryless addends; their values are the exact enum mode.
Modal validates environment values and the native-CLMAD prerequisite before image creation; the image environment and baked build retain the mode.
The baked identity, buildFor requested identity, real rebuild command and runBench no-rebuild guard include the integer mode, so stale binaries cannot be reused after a mode change.
Benchmark identity, benchmark/autotune rows and compile-check records preserve the selected integer mode, while nonpacked records remain None.
checkPackedReduction rejects missing, wrong, malformed or duplicate markers without restoring a previously invalid sample; invalid rates become zero.

packed_audit forwards the same mode into its arithmetic build, records expected/actual values, and rejects arithmetic identity failure before integration or timing. Every timed sample reaches the shared marker/count gate.
The fixture correction supplies the new default variable and its new output marker. It does not relax a production predicate; additional mutation tests exercise the new rejection cases.
Documentation distinguishes canonical inputs, host simulation, compiler evidence and pending device validation/timing.
limits: Only relevant Python wrapper/count tests were executed by this review; no C++/CUDA compile, numerical field suite, GPU job or job-status poll was performed.
The seven preprocessor tests were inspected and their owner-reported pass was not rerun. The unchanged report tests outside this scope are not counted among the38 tests run here.
The arithmetic header is covered by the prior canonical-input algebra/header/CPU review. FUSED2 masks top limbs, so arbitrary noncanonical raw input equivalence is not claimed.
Public GPU correctness and throughput remain pending at this review boundary. The private GPU run uses different marker labels and does not by itself validate public wrapper execution.
Source-level and static compiler instruction counts are not a speedup measurement; nonzero modes remain opt-in.
